district_center_rule: Each town must define either portal_hub for the central portal district or district_anchor for normal neighborhoods/districts.
grid_coordinate_format: [x, y] integer list within town grid bounds
notes: Authored town files are safe to hand-edit as JSON.
Runtime save/state files must not overwrite these authored town definitions.
Blocks can reference schedule nodes by block id; validators resolve those references before runtime use.
Normal towns should use neighbor_towns to describe connections without hardcoding runtime teleports.
Market/social towns should include vendor, courier, guard, public gathering, and alert/shelter schedule nodes before full NPC AI is attached.
Security/control towns should include checkpoint, patrol, shelter, command, and alert-lockdown schedule nodes before full NPC AI is attached.
Controlled-access towns can use access_level="controlled" and event hooks to redirect civilians while guards move to patrol/checkpoint nodes.
Industrial towns should include work, repair, supply, courier, shelter, and command nodes so future NPC schedules can redirect during power/supply alerts.
Harbor/waterfront towns should include dock, ferry, water utility, public boardwalk, shelter, scan/checkpoint, and storm/ocean alert schedule nodes before full NPC AI is attached.
Water-edge towns should keep ocean/future water cells explicit so later rendering can preserve water transitions without confusing NPC land routes.
Archive/MatrixCore towns should include public archive, memory, research, restricted, shelter, courier, and lore-pulse nodes before narrative NPC AI is attached.
Archive towns can mix public and restricted blocks, but restricted destinations must remain explicit schedule nodes so lockdown and guard routing can override normal schedules safely.
Pass 8 normalizes all authored town grids to a shared 10x8 district frame before neighborhood detailing starts.
city_grid_atlas.json is the city-level placement authority; town JSON files remain the local block/schedule authority.
Neighborhood build passes should add detail inside the existing even district frame rather than changing grid_size again.
Pass 9 starts neighborhood buildout in Residential Alpha using data/database/utopia/neighborhoods/residential_alpha_neighborhood_01.json.
Neighborhood files add lots, addresses, porches, rooms, and micro-schedule nodes without changing the town grid frame.
Pass 14 adds district-specific structure variants and purpose layers so every block has an understandable use before deeper building art is authored.
Blocks now expose structure_variant_id, purpose_id, activity_affordances, and interior_policy for future NPC schedules and highlight-only interiors.
Structure variants should stay data-driven and district-appropriate: civic/portal, residential, market, security, industrial, harbor, and archive areas each use their own catalog.
Pass 15 makes all district town blocks renderable as 3D purpose massing, including non-building blocks represented as open-space, water-edge, gate, plaza, or service volumes.
structure_massing_profile.visual_policy.no_arbitrary_diagonals must stay true; floor bands and verticals are outer-perimeter only so lines do not cut through buildings without purpose.
Detailed interiors remain highlight-only and separate from exterior massing; runtime should not load all interiors at once.
Pass 16 completes the city atlas to a 3x3 district grid.
Every new district must include structure_variant_profile and structure_massing_profile on each block before citizens/schedules rely on it.

canonical_grid_rule.purpose: Keep district frames even before building detailed neighborhoods.

neighborhood_rule.purpose: Detailed living-world blocks are now layered inside towns through safe-edit neighborhood files.

structure_variant_rule.purpose: Each district exposes purpose layers and structure variants appropriate to its identity before individual buildings are modeled in detail.
structure_variant_rule.block_rule: Every town block references a variant and purpose from its district profile.
structure_variant_rule.visual_rule: Variant metadata is semantic first: rendering must still keep foundations clean and avoid meaningless line crossings.
structure_variant_rule.interior_rule: interior_policy must be exterior_only, highlight_only, or locked_until_story.

structure_massing_rule.visual_contract: foundation first, outer perimeter lines only, no arbitrary diagonals, highlight-only interiors
